dialogue.t: Oh? I suppose our commissions here at Tales of Humanity are too easy for you... Or have you been in dire need of Mora lately?

dialogue.sit: Well, you can never have enough Mora.
A little bit of column A, a little bit of column B.

dialogue.t: Mm-hmm. A most common sentiment.
If there's one thing we don't lack here, it's work to be done. In fact, The Steambird could probably be considered the largest clearinghouse for jobs outside of the Adventurers' Guild.
Well, I say that, but we didn't really need to take up the social services aspect.
Whatever the case, since you need Mora, allow me to recommend a certain long-term gig to you.
This is a note that Mr. Leroy left with us over half a year ago — most of us who live on this street know him well.
Although his reputation when he was younger was less than stellar, I haven't heard any untoward rumors concerning him in recent years.
He's been alone most of his life, and with his only daughter not being by his side, there's no one to take care of him... I suppose that's where a person could use an hourly worker to help.
From what I know, he's not hard up for Mora, so you'll be well-paid.
It's a nearly danger-free job with great compensation to boot. No reason not to consider it.
So we just need to help him with some housework, right? Paimon thinks that sounds pretty chill!

dialogue.sit: Please give me his address, if you would.

dialogue.t: Of course. Just turn two corners, and loop around... Actually, never mind. Let me give you a map instead.
Remember to tell him that I was the one to introduce you, alright?
Athos's shirt, 1,000 Mora... Morticia's necklace... Tsk, tsk. Youngsters these days sure know how to spend.
Hey there! Euphrasie sent us.

dialogue.sit: You explain to Mr. Leroy why you're here.

dialogue.t: Haha, that was half a year ago, wasn't it? I didn't think Euphrasie would hold on to that commission for so long.
It's true — I did think of hiring hourly workers. After all, even the most capable of us get old and need others to take care of them.
I spent so much of my life working to have this home, but in my old age, I found that I had no one to share it with.
That did make me quite sad for a time — so it's a good thing, all in all, that my daughter and son-in-law have come to take care of me.
They're good children, they love each other very much, and they keep me company. There's nothing more that I could want.
That's to say, youngster, that I'm not hiring anymore.

dialogue.sit: So we came here for nothing...?

dialogue.t: Well, now, don't be too down. That's not how young'uns should be. You lot should be enjoying your best life, armed with a smile!
Also, since you made the trip here, and since Euphrasie recommended you, I do, in fact, have some work for you.
It just so happens that the kids are out, and I can't quite handle everything here. Of course, you will be paid.
Ooh, nice! You're a great guy, Mr. Leroy!
Hahaha, and you've got quite the silver tongue!
Alright, then, go help me clean the stains by the door and behind the house — and feed Nana some fish while you're at it.
Right, I forgot to mention, but Nana's my cat — you know, the one by the door. Thanks in advance on Nana's behalf.
Well, that sounds simple enough. No problem! Leave it to us.
Did you forget what I'd asked you to do? ...Ah, children and their memories.
The first thing I asked you to help with is to clean near the entrance and the back of the house. The next is to feed a bit of fish to Nana, my cat.
You're done?
That's right, Mr. Leroy. Also...
Hmm? What is it? Want some candy? Or would you like your pocket money now?
B—Both, hehehe...
Haha, what a greedy little child. Still, that's fine — that's exactly what little children should be like.
Especially little ladies as cute as you, Paimon. Macarons, pretty dresses, and lovely homes — that's what you deserve to have.
Hehe, Paimon reckons so too! Hey, {NICKNAME}, could we get...
Boo! Boo! You're so stingy!

dialogue.sit: Don't lose sight of why we're traveling, Paimon...

dialogue.t: Paimon doesn't see how any of that stuff conflicts with having macarons, skirts, or big beautiful houses, though...
Heh, what's with the sudden argument? Tsk, kids. But a little banter now and then is good. That just shows that you're still children.

dialogue.sit: That's how you know we get along.

dialogue.t: Treasure your childhood. It won't last.
...Anyway, here — candies and coins both. Now then, do behave, alright?
Yay, snacks! Thank you, Mr. Leroy!
Just call me Benoit, child. Leroy is my surname.
I am the last Leroy in the entire Court of Fontaine — mentions of my family name make this poor old soul quite lonely indeed, so please, just use my name.
Mr. Le... Er, Benoit, so... Your daughter doesn't share your surname?
Morticia isn't my daughter by blood. I took her in half a year ago. That said, she may as well be my own trueborn daughter.
If you don't mind, you can come again tomorrow — she and Athos should be back by then.
I'm sure she won't mind having two lovely children like you over for snacks, especially since you're helping us with some of the chores.
Some other children come by occasionally, so feel free to play with them, too. I love children — the more of them are around, the merrier the house is.
If you don't see me when you come over again, just knock and ask for me — Athos will open the door for you.
Alrighty! We'll be back tomorrow, then!
Good, good, I should be going back inside, at any rate.
See you then, children.
